description: EARNED source authority. A source's rank is DERIVED from its publisher/domain (and whether its provenance is verified/signed), NOT assigned as a number on an artifact. scripts/artifact_graph/source_authority.classify() resolves a (publisher, source_uri, signed) into a tier+rank+lineage; reconciliation reads rank from there. Longest/most-specific domain match wins, on a domain-segment boundary (a true subdomain or exact host) so a look-alike like 'sec.gov.attacker.com' never earns sec.gov's authority. Each rule carries an 'authority_id' family so multi-source corroboration counts one real authority ONCE even across its many subdomains (e.g. OFAC's sanctionssearch.ofac.treas.gov + ofac.treasury.gov = one voice); the bare '.gov'/'.mil' catch-alls carry none and fall back to the domain. A top-tier domain whose provenance is NOT verified is DOWNGRADED (claimed != verified). An unlisted publisher earns 'unverified' (rank 10) — never a neutral default. To grant a source authority, add a publisher rule here; never hand-type a source_rank on an artifact.

source_of_law.definition: binding primary text: statute / regulation / the codified eCFR or Federal Register rule

official_agency.definition: the regulating agency's own authoritative publication (CFPB, OFAC/Treasury, FDA, BIS, SEC)

official_guidance.definition: agency guidance / FAQ / bulletin — interpretive, not binding (also: a CLAIMED top-tier source whose provenance is unverified)

government_other.definition: a .gov source not matched to a more specific tier

standards_body.definition: a recognized standards body / SRO (FINRA, NIST, ISO)

secondary_summary.definition: law-firm memo, vendor summary, trade press — derivative, not authoritative

unverified.definition: unknown / unsigned / unlisted publisher — earns no authority

notes: signed=true marks a publisher whose provenance is officially/cryptographically verifiable at ingest. classify(signed=...) carries the per-SOURCE verification result; a source matched to source_of_law/official_agency but signed=False is DOWNGRADED to official_guidance (claimed authority, unverified provenance) so the gate never grants binding authority to an unverified claim. Add a publisher to grant authority; this file is the ONLY place a domain→authority mapping lives. 'authority_id' groups one real authority's domains/subdomains into a single corroboration voice (so two reads of the same agency cannot inflate 'independent authorities agree'); omit it on catch-all suffix rules so they stay distinct by domain.
